newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-LIONS PROP SMITH SHOULD BE FIT FOR SECOND TEST.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LIONS PROP SMITH SHOULD BE FIT FOR SECOND TEST.

text.p: British Lions prop Tom Smith, who limped out of the first test victory over South Africa on Saturday, is expected to have recovered in time for the second test in Durban on Saturday.
Smith twisted an ankle during the 25-16 victory at Newlands but two days rest was all he required to recover, Lions manager Fran Cotton said on Sunday.
Flyhalf Gregor Townsend, who was feared to have broken ribs during the game, is suffering from severe bruising but should also be fit for the second test, Cotton added.
The rest of the Lions squad , including Saturday's victorious test team , trained in Cape Town on Sunday morning.

"The test boys wanted to support the boys who will play on Tuesday against Free State," said Cotton. "That came from the players. It's typical of the incredible squad unity that has got us so far on this tour."
The training session followed a team meeting at which the Lions' ultimate objective of winning the series was reiterated.
"To win the first test was very important but it's the first team to win two tests that takes the series," Cotton said.
The Lions will announce their team to meet Free State on Monday and are expected to name the side for the second test on Wednesday.
